title: Statusline Settings
description: Shape of $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.statusline-settings (default ~/.claude/.statusline-settings), the single config store shared by .claude/statusline-command.sh (the renderer) and scripts/claude/statusline-settings.js (the writer, fronted by /statusline-options). Editor autocomplete and test-time checks only: nothing validates against this at runtime, because a settings file that fails validation must still render a statusline rather than break the prompt. Both readers degrade silently to the defaults declared here instead.

style.description: verbose spells the effort/caveman/ponytail indicators out as labels; compact renders them as badges.

nerd_font.description: Whether the terminal has a Nerd Font. false falls the git status icons back to glyphs any font has (↑ ahead, ^ staged-new, + untracked, ~ modified, - deleted, and "git" for the group's leading branch icon); the clean mark stays ✓ (U+2713), which is ordinary Unicode rather than a Nerd Font glyph and renders without one. Colours are identical in both modes — only the glyph changes. Top-level rather than a section because it hides nothing: it changes how a group draws, not whether it draws. Defaults true and is user-declared because font support is not detectable from a terminal; no TERM_PROGRAM/WT_SESSION heuristic can tell a real glyph from a tofu box.

weekly.description: SUPERSEDED alias for sections.seven_day, still read so files written by older versions keep working. sections.seven_day wins when both are present, and the next write drops this key. Files in the wild may also hold the strings "on"/"off" (the shape this key was originally written in); both readers accept them, this schema declares only the boolean because that is the form still worth writing.

badge.description: Raw badge string, ANSI-capable, prepended to line 1. Empty string is treated as absent, which is what makes the renderer fall back to the superseded statusline-badge.txt. No default: absent means no badge from here.

sections.description: Per-section visibility. false omits the section entirely, leaving no separator or double space behind.

context.description: The bar/percentage/window-size run inside the model bracket. false still renders a bare [Model]: the model name has no gate of its own.

five_hour.description: The [5h] rate-limit group. Also omitted regardless when the session input carries no five_hour data (API-key auth).

seven_day.description: The [7d] weekly rate-limit group. The one section defaulting off — opt-in via /statusline-options weekly=true.

advisor.description: The [advisor:<model>] marker, read from advisorModel in the config dir's settings.json.

caveman.description: The caveman-mode indicator, read from the .caveman-active flag file.

ponytail.description: The ponytail-mode indicator, read from the .ponytail-active flag file.

git.description: The line-2 git group: repo, branch, status icons and the worktree marker. The project name is not part of it and always renders.

session_start_date.description: The whole line-2 clock group: icon, session start time and duration. Set via /statusline-options clock=false.

agent.description: The agent label at the head of line 1. true shows it whenever the session input carries .agent.name, which today means subagents only — that restriction is what the data does, not a rule the renderer applies. A boolean rather than a tri-state for exactly that reason: with no input that distinguishes "always" from "subagents only", a third state would document an intent nothing implements.
